episode_title: News Roundup 23/10/26: Hemnet Q3, Compass Sues CRMLS & Zillow Comes to Claude

real_qa.q: Why did Hemnet Q3 results show declines in listings and profitability yet the stock price jumped 10-11%?
real_qa.r: Hemnet's Q3 results showed total listings down, paid listings down 30%, published listings down 13%, and operating profit down 30% year-over-year due to a shift to a sell now, pay later business model. However, the market had set expectations so low that Hemnet beat consensus on all profit measures, causing the share price to jump 10-11% because the market viewed performance as better than anticipated despite internal metrics declining.
real_qa.requete: Hemnet Q3 results stock price jump 2026

real_qa.q: What is Compass suing CRMLS over and what fines do agents face?
real_qa.r: Compass sued CRMLS, the California MLS, alleging anti-competitive rules that punish agents for publicly marketing homes per lawful client instructions. Under CRMLS rules, if a homeowner markets a home anywhere on the internet, the listing must be given to CRMLS within one business day, and agents who violate this by following lawful client instructions face fines up to $2,500 per violation, suspension or expulsion from the MLS. Compass stated it will pay any fines levied against agents affected by these rules.
real_qa.requete: Compass CRMLS lawsuit MLS fines agents

real_qa.q: How does Zillow's Claude integration improve upon its previous ChatGPT integration for real estate search?
real_qa.r: Zillow's Claude integration performs noticeably better than the ChatGPT integration tested in January. For queries like wheelchair-friendly apartments in Seattle, Claude admits Zillow lacks that filter but pulls related listings and intelligently evaluates which are actual matches. For apartments above the third floor in New York City, Claude uses proxy filtering by floor description rather than just keyword matching, adding interpretive value that the basic Zillow interface would not provide.
real_qa.requete: Zillow Claude integration real estate search

real_qa.q: What is the distinction between AI as a search tool versus AI as a companion in real estate decision-making?
real_qa.r: The distinction is whether AI actively performs the search for you or acts as a companion and co-pilot alongside your decision. For transactional purchases like finding a replacement lamp, users can outsource the search to AI entirely. However, buying a house is an emotional decision where users should not outsource the search to AI but rather use it as a companion—like Simon Bray's Klein-Azigen Real Estate companion model—to provide feedback, cut through noise, and help avoid bad decisions while the user remains in control.
real_qa.requete: AI companion versus search tool real estate

real_qa.q: What components determine trust in a real estate portal according to real estate industry leaders?
real_qa.r: Trust in a portal equals a function of multiple factors: time in market and reputation (portals operating 30 years have built trust; some European portals trace reputation back to newspapers with 50 years' history), the data presented (clearly identifying overpriced vs underpriced properties), business model transparency (if overly reliant on agents, people sense it), volume of listings, and consistent market feedback. The easiest factor to replicate is time—you simply need to be around long enough that people grow up using you.
